notes: Measured on 1061 human and 577 AI held-out samples that were not used to set the thresholds. Shorter samples are excerpts of longer documents, so there are 375 distinct human and 210 distinct AI documents behind them.
Non-native English writers: 0 of 470 wrongly flagged (0.0%, 95% range 0.0%-0.8%); this meets the 1% go-public gate on the point estimate.
With about 1061 human samples, a 1% false-flag rate can only be measured roughly (95% range for the overall figure: 0.1%-0.8%).
Not tested against gemini text: none was available for this run.
Length matters: AI text was caught 0.0% of the time at 20-49 words, 1.0% at 50-149 words and 18.1% at 150+ words.

AI samples were written by each model on its own (default model, via the vendor's command-line app, several pieces per request). Edited, paraphrased or 'humanized' AI text was not tested; expect misses there.

Human samples were written before ChatGPT existed: US school essays, English-learner essays, TOEFL practice essays, 1990s Reuters news and Reddit short stories. Other kinds of writing (technical, legal, poetry, very formal or formulaic text) were not tested.
On 31 documents that mix human and AI paragraphs, the '% AI' estimate was off by 48 percentage points on average.
